Throne of God
throhn uhv god
noun
From throne + God; the seat and symbol of the LORD’s sovereign rule over all things.

📖 Biblical Definition

The throne of God is the seat and symbol of the LORD’s sovereign, eternal rule over all that He has made. The LORD hath prepared his throne in the heavens; and his kingdom ruleth over all. Heaven is His throne, and the earth His footstool; He sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers. The prophets beheld it: Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the seraphim crying, Holy, holy, holy; Ezekiel saw the likeness of a throne above the firmament; Daniel saw the Ancient of days sit, His throne like the fiery flame; and John saw a throne set in heaven, and One that sat thereon, encircled by a rainbow and worshipped by the living creatures and the elders day and night. The throne is a throne of holiness, of justice, and of grace—justice and judgment are the habitation of His throne—and to it the believer is bidden come boldly, that he may find grace to help, for the throne of judgment has become, through Christ, a throne of grace. From the throne proceeds the river of the water of life; before it the redeemed shall stand and serve. The dictionary honors the throne of God as the great symbol of His sovereignty, holiness, and grace—the seat from which He governs all things, judges all men, and dispenses mercy to His people through the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The seat and symbol of the LORD’s sovereign, eternal rule; a throne of holiness, justice, and—through Christ—grace, to which the believer comes boldly.

expand to see more

THRONE OF GOD, the seat and symbol of the LORD’s sovereign rule.

His throne is in the heavens; His kingdom ruleth over all (Psa 103:19).

Beheld by Isaiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, and John in glory.

A throne of holiness and justice; justice is its habitation.

Through Christ, a throne of grace, to which we come boldly (Heb 4:16).

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 103:19 — "The LORD hath prepared his throne in the heavens; and his kingdom ruleth over all."

Isa 6:1 — "In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple."

Heb 4:16 — "Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need."

Rev 4:2 — "And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The throne of God is reduced to mere imagery or emptied of His real sovereignty; Scripture sets it as the seat of His holy rule, justice, and saving grace.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the modern instinct to treat the throne of God as mere poetic imagery, a figure emptied of its reality—as though God did not truly reign, or His sovereignty were a metaphor we may take or leave. But the prophets and apostles beheld the throne as the most solid of realities: Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up (Isa 6:1), and John saw a throne set in heaven, and One that sat upon it (Rev 4:2). The throne is the symbol of a rule that is actual, absolute, and eternal.

The principle to recover is the union of sovereignty, holiness, justice, and grace in the throne. The LORD hath prepared His throne in the heavens, and His kingdom ruleth over all (Psa 103:19)—nothing is outside His government. It is a throne of holiness, before which the seraphim veil their faces and cry, Holy, holy, holy; and a throne of justice, for justice and judgment are its habitation. Yet—wonder of the gospel—through the blood of Christ the throne of judgment has become for the believer a throne of grace, to which he is bidden come boldly, that he may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need (Heb 4:16). The throne that the wicked must dread is the very throne where the saint finds mercy.

Throne + God; the seat of the LORD’s sovereign, holy, just rule, become through Christ a throne of grace to which the believer comes boldly.
